Growth assessment 2026-Q2 · Eurostat quarterly national accounts
Executive assessmentReal GDP grew 3.8% year-on-year in 2026-Q2 and the growth mix is classified as consumption-led growth. The largest positive engine was household consumption, while the contribution mix is assessed as mixed. Domestic demand contributed +5.4 pp and net exports -2.0 pp. The decomposition covers 100% of the six core expenditure components. The component sum differs from headline GDP growth by +0.4 pp, so the decomposition should be read with caution. Watchpoints: Contribution reconciliation gap +0.35 pp; Import-intensive domestic demand; Investment supporting growth; Strong household-demand contribution.

Executive structural synthesis

Lithuania's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as cautious / mixed with structural pressure. Growth Quality: Consumption-led growth. Investment Quality: Construction-heavy. Competitiveness: Productivity gains with labour-cost pressure. Household Demand: Broad-based household demand. External Sector: External drag on growth. Across the five modules, 1 are favourable, 2 mixed/neutral and 2 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as construction-heavy. GFCF stood at 22.4% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 42.6% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 57.1%. Total real GFCF growth was +7.3% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Strong real GFCF growth.

The current structural signal is classified as productivity gains with labour-cost pressure. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q2), real labour productivity per hour grew +2.7% year-on-year versus +0.8% in EU-27. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +5.8% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Elevated NULC growth; Large productivity gap versus EU; Large NULC gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as broad-based household demand. Real household consumption grew +4.5% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 9.3% of nominal household expenditure and services for 40.2% in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Strong services consumption growth.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as external drag on growth. Net exports contributed -1.96 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Exports contributed +3.79 pp and imports -5.75 pp. Real exports grew +5.2% YoY while real imports grew +8.4% YoY. Watchpoints: Domestic demand accompanied by import drag.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
